# FireLab MCP tools

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:tools` from src/mcp/server.ts. Edit the tool definitions, not this file. -->

FireLab's MCP server (`firelab mcp`) exposes 24 tools and 3 prompts. Every tool takes an optional `device` (adb serial or IP); with exactly one device connected you can leave it out. Results are JSON (as text and as `structuredContent`); `screenshot` returns an image. Errors come back as tool errors with a hint, e.g. `Device 192.168.1.50:5555 has not authorized this computer. Look at the TV and accept the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt [unauthorized]`.

Annotations: **read-only** tools never change the device; tools marked **changes the device** say what they change.

## Devices

### `list_devices` (read-only)

Lists Fire TV / Android TV devices known to adb with their state ("device" = ready, "unauthorized" = someone must press Allow on the TV, "offline", "connecting"), model, friendly name (e.g. "Fire TV Stick 4K Plus"), Fire OS version, CPU ABI, RAM, GPU and the quality tier FireLab suggests for it. Start here.

No parameters.

### `scan_network` (read-only)

Scans the local network (the /24 of each network interface, or the given subnet) for devices with ADB over Wi-Fi on port 5555 and checks they speak adb. Does not connect to anything and never triggers a prompt on other devices; use connect_device on a result. Takes about 2-5 seconds.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subnet` | string |  | CIDR range, e.g. "192.168.1.0/24". Default: this computer's local /24 networks. |

### `connect_device` (acts on the device)

Connects to a device over Wi-Fi (adb connect) and keeps it connected (FireLab reconnects automatically if Wi-Fi drops). The first time, the TV shows "Allow USB debugging?": a person must select Allow (tick "Always allow"); until then the state is "unauthorized". Requires Developer options > ADB debugging ON on the device.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip` | string | yes | IP address, optionally with port: "192.168.1.50" or "192.168.1.50:5555". |

### `device_info` (read-only)

Details of one device: model and friendly name, Fire OS / Android version, API level, ABIs (most Fire TV Sticks are 32-bit armeabi-v7a), RAM, screen resolution and density, SoC, GPU (the real WebGL renderer once a WebView has been inspected), suggested quality tier, whether the screen is awake or showing the screensaver, and the foreground app.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |

### `wake_device` (acts on the device)

Wakes the device from sleep or the screensaver (KEYCODE_WAKEUP, which does not act inside the foreground app) and confirms via the power manager. Use before screenshots or key presses if the screen may be off.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |

## Remote and screen

### `press_keys` (acts on the device)

Presses Fire TV remote buttons in order. Keys: up, down, left, right, ok, back, home, menu, playpause, rewind, fastforward, volup, voldown, mute, search, wake ("ok" is the center/select button). Modifiers: "down*3" presses three times, "ok:long" is a long press, "right:1500" holds for 1.5 s. Plain presses with gapMs 0 are sent in one batch (about 1 s on a Fire TV Stick); set gapMs (e.g. 300) when an app needs time between presses (animations, page loads). Take a screenshot afterwards to see the result.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `keys` | string[] | yes | e.g. ["down", "down", "ok"] or ["right:1500"] |
| `gapMs` | integer |  | Pause between presses in ms (default 0). |
| `holdMs` | integer |  | Hold every key this long (ms), for games that read key-down time. |

### `type_text` (acts on the device)

Types text into the focused text field (adb input text). Plain ASCII only. Focus a field first (press_keys "ok" on it). For WebView pages you can also set values with webview_eval.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `text` | string | yes |  |

### `screenshot` (read-only)

Captures the TV screen as a JPEG image (default 960 px wide, enough to read UI text). DRM-protected video shows black. Capture takes about 1-2.5 s over Wi-Fi.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `width` | integer |  | Image width in px (default 960). |
| `quality` | integer |  | JPEG quality (default 70). |

## Apps

### `list_apps` (read-only)

Lists third-party (user-installed) apps with version and whether they have a launcher entry (launchable). Launchable apps come first.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |

### `install_app` (changes the device)

CHANGES THE DEVICE: installs an APK file from this computer (adb install -r), replacing an existing install of the same app but keeping its data. Checks first that the APK's native code matches the device CPU (Fire TV Sticks are 32-bit ARM) and its minSdk. Returns the package name.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `path` | string | yes | Path to the .apk on this computer. |

### `launch_app` (acts on the device)

Wakes the device and starts an app on its TV (Leanback) launcher activity, or brings it to the front if it is running. Optional url is passed in the intent as data and as a "url" string extra (for WebView wrappers that read it). Returns the pid and the launch time Android reports.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string | yes | Android package name, e.g. "com.example.game" (see list_apps). |
| `url` | string |  | Optional URL for apps that accept one (intent data + "url" extra). |
| `activity` | string |  | Explicit component, e.g. "com.example/.MainActivity". Default: the launcher activity. |

### `stop_app` (changes the device)

CHANGES APP STATE: force-stops an app (am force-stop). Its process ends and unsaved in-app progress is lost; installed data and saves stay. Use to restart an app cleanly.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string | yes | Android package name, e.g. "com.example.game" (see list_apps). |

### `reset_app` (changes the device)

DELETES ALL OF THE APP'S DATA (pm clear): saves, logins, settings and caches, so the next launch is a true first run. Cannot be undone. Only use on apps you are testing, never on a person's own apps, and only when asked. Requires confirm: true.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string | yes | Android package name, e.g. "com.example.game" (see list_apps). |
| `confirm` | `true` | yes | Must be true: acknowledges that all app data is deleted. |

## WebView (Chrome DevTools)

### `webview_eval` (acts on the device)

Runs a JavaScript expression in the page inside an app's WebView (over Chrome DevTools via adb) and returns its JSON value; promises are awaited. Great for reading game/app state, document.title, location.href, navigator.userAgent, or checking the DOM. The app must enable WebView debugging (WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true), usually in debug builds). Prefer read-only expressions; never loop inside the page waiting for UI state (it can freeze the page); poll from outside with repeated calls instead.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `expression` | string | yes | e.g. "document.title" or "({ url: location.href, w: innerWidth })" |
| `package` | string |  | App whose WebView to use. Default: the foreground app, else any debuggable WebView. |
| `timeoutMs` | integer |  | Default 10000. |

### `webview_console` (read-only)

Console messages and uncaught exceptions from the page in an app's WebView, recorded from the moment FireLab connected. Use waitMs to collect for a few seconds (e.g. while you press keys in another call), minLevel "warn" or "error" to focus on problems.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string |  |  |
| `minLevel` | `debug` \| `log` \| `info` \| `warn` \| `error` |  |  |
| `since` | number |  | Only entries after this epoch-ms timestamp. |
| `limit` | integer |  | Default 200 (newest). |
| `waitMs` | integer |  | Collect for this long before returning. |

## Performance

### `measure_performance` (read-only)

Measures the running app for a few seconds without changing anything: frame rate (median and p10 of per-second fps: from window.firelab if the page uses @firelab/perf, else by counting frames that draw WebGL / requestAnimationFrame; for apps without a WebView, such as Unity or native games, from SurfaceFlinger frame timing), memory (app + WebView renderer PSS in MB), CPU (% of one core, like top) and free device memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string |  | Default: the foreground app. |
| `seconds` | integer |  | Default 10. |
| `fpsExpr` | string |  | Optional JS expression returning the app's own fps number, e.g. "window.game.stats.fps". |

### `performance_sweep` (acts on the device)

For a WebView app or web game: loads the page at each quality tier (url?q=low, ?q=tv, ...), warms up, measures fps and memory, and recommends the richest tier that holds the target (default: median >= 30 fps within 5%, p10 >= 24) with a reason and a markdown table. Reloads the page several times and restores the original URL at the end. Takes about (warmupS + sampleS + load time) per tier: around 2 minutes for 3 tiers.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `url` | string | yes | The page URL the app loads, e.g. "http://192.168.1.20:4173/". The tier parameter is added. |
| `package` | string |  | The app hosting the WebView (launched if not running). Default: the foreground app's WebView. |
| `tiers` | string[] |  | Lightest to richest. Default ["low", "tv", "tv-hd", "high"]. |
| `param` | string |  | URL parameter name for the tier (default "q"). |
| `warmupS` | number |  | Seconds to wait after load before measuring (default 8). |
| `sampleS` | number |  | Seconds to measure per tier (default 15). |
| `targetFps` | number |  | Default 30. |
| `minP10` | number |  | Default 80% of targetFps. |
| `actionKeys` | string[] |  | Remote keys to press after each load to reach a busy scene, e.g. ["ok", "down", "ok"]. |
| `actionEval` | string |  | JS to run after each load to reach a busy scene (awaited). |
| `fpsExpr` | string |  | JS expression returning the app's own fps, if it has a meter. |

## Play sessions and logs

### `watch_start` (acts on the device)

Starts recording while a PERSON plays on the TV with the real remote: every remote press (via getevent; keys you send with press_keys are not recorded), fps / memory / CPU every few seconds, console errors, and a thumbnail every 10 s. Call watch_stop for the summary. One session per device.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string |  | App to measure. Default: the foreground app. |
| `intervalMs` | integer |  | Perf sample interval (default 3000). |
| `thumbEveryS` | integer |  | Thumbnail interval in seconds (default 10, 0 = none). |

### `watch_stop` (acts on the device)

Stops the play session recording and returns the summary: number of key presses and the most used keys, fps median / p10, peak memory, error count and first errors, thumbnail files and the folder with the full timeline (timeline.jsonl).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |

### `logcat` (read-only)

Recent Android log lines (logcat), optionally only from one app's process, at or above a level, or with a tag containing some text. Useful for native crashes (level "error"), ANRs and WebView renderer crashes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string |  | Only this app's process. |
| `lines` | integer |  | Default 100. |
| `level` | `verbose` \| `debug` \| `info` \| `warn` \| `error` \| `fatal` |  | Minimum level. |
| `tag` | string |  | Only tags containing this text (case-insensitive). |

## Game testing engine

### `explore_start` (acts on the device)

Starts FireLab's game-testing engine in the background: it plays the app with the remote (Go-Explore: returns to promising screens and tries every key there, plus fast repeats and long presses), walks the D-pad focus on every new screen, and watches for crashes, ANRs, JS exceptions, black screens, frozen pictures or a stopped render loop, focus traps, unreachable controls and non-spatial D-pad moves. Afterwards it shrinks each finding to the shortest key sequence that reproduces it and writes report.html. Presses keys and relaunches the app for the whole run: don't use the TV meanwhile. Returns a runId for explore_status / explore_findings / explore_stop. Refuses com.sunsetvilla.tv.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string |  | adb serial or IP of the device, e.g. "192.168.1.50:5555" or "192.168.1.50". Optional when only one device is connected. |
| `package` | string |  | Android package name of the app to explore, e.g. "com.example.game" (see list_apps). Not needed with driver "demo". |
| `url` | string |  | For a wrapped web app (firelab wrap): the page to open, passed as the launch intent's url extra. |
| `minutes` | number |  | Exploration time (default 10). Shrinking runs afterwards. |
| `steps` | integer |  | Stop after this many steps instead. |
| `seed` | integer |  | Random seed (default 1); the same seed repeats the same choices. |
| `keys` | `up` \| `down` \| `left` \| `right` \| `ok` \| `back` \| `menu` \| `playpause` \| `rewind` \| `fastforward` \| `home` \| `search`[] |  | Remote keys to use (default up down left right ok back menu playpause, rewind/fastforward rarely). |
| `oracles` | `health` \| `screen` \| `focus`[] |  | Default all three. |
| `stateExpr` | string |  | JS expression returning small JSON app state, e.g. "({mode: game.mode})"; makes states sharper. |
| `focusSelector` | string |  | CSS selector of the focused control for apps that draw focus with a class, e.g. ".focused". |
| `strategy` | `explore` \| `random` |  | "random" is the monkey baseline for comparisons. |
| `minimize` | boolean |  | Shrink findings afterwards (default true). |
| `minimizeMinutes` | number |  | Shrink budget per finding (default 20). |
| `emulateGpu` | string |  | A Fire TV model id (e.g. "AFTSSS"): WebGL in the app reports only that model's GPU features and limits (WebGL2, max texture size, extensions, compressed formats, shader precision), not its speed; every WebGL call that fails becomes a gpu-unsupported finding. Useful on the emulator lab, which has the model's RAM and screen but not its GPU. Needs a debuggable WebView. |
| `driver` | `adb` \| `vda` \| `demo` |  | "adb" (default): Fire OS / Android TV. "vda": Vega OS over the Vega SDK's `vega` CLI; device is then a `vega exec vda devices` serial. Vega has no JS evaluation and FireLab sees the app go only when its process ends; states come from the screen. Not yet run on a real Vega device or the Vega Virtual Device. "demo": Lantern Lake, a simulated TV game with 6 seeded bugs that runs inside FireLab (no device needed; 10 minutes of device time take a few seconds): use it to try FireLab. |

### `explore_status` (read-only)

Progress of an exploration run: status (running, minimizing, reporting, done, failed, stopped), steps, distinct states, findings per severity, the coverage curve (states over seconds), the current screen (as an image) and, when done, the report path and exit code.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | string | yes | From explore_start. |

### `explore_stop` (acts on the device)

Stops an exploration run (it keeps what it found, skips shrinking and writes the report). Returns the summary.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | string | yes |  |

### `explore_findings` (read-only)

The findings of an exploration run (running or finished), most severe first: oracle, kind, title, detail, reproduction status and rate, and the key sequence that reproduces it (shrunk when shrinking ran), plus the screenshot of the first ones as images. Replay one with `firelab replay <trace>`.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | string | yes |  |
| `minSeverity` | `critical` \| `major` \| `minor` \| `info` |  | Default minor (info findings such as "plateau" are left out). |

## Prompts

### `playtest`

Walks through a full play-test on a real device: launch, navigate with the remote, look for visual and console problems, measure performance, report.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `package` | yes | Package of the app or game to test. |
| `goal` |  | What to try, e.g. "start a new game and play the first level". |
| `device` |  |  |

### `tune_performance`

Runs a quality-tier sweep for a WebView app or web game, explains the result, and suggests changes.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `url` | yes | The page URL the app loads, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:4173/ |
| `package` |  |  |
| `tiers` |  | Comma-separated, lightest first. Default "low,tv,tv-hd,high". |
| `device` |  |  |

### `explore_app`

Runs FireLab's game-testing engine on an app, reads the findings and summarises them for the developer with repro keys.

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `package` | yes | Package of the app or game to test. |
| `minutes` |  | Exploration time in minutes (default 10). |
| `device` |  |  |

## Key names

`up down left right ok back home menu playpause rewind fastforward volup voldown mute search wake` (`ok` is the center button). Also accepted: `select`, `enter`, `ff`, `rew`, Android key codes (`66`) and names (`KEYCODE_CHANNEL_UP`). Modifiers: `down*3` (three presses), `ok:long` (long press), `right:1500` (hold 1.5 s).

## Same features over HTTP and the CLI

The dashboard API (`firelab ui`, http://localhost:7300/api) and the CLI (`firelab help`) expose the same operations; see [CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md) for the HTTP routes and payloads.
